findings.summary: Review point 3 (PR-13, ENG-TRUST-1): a task with writes can end GROUNDED. Two checks are enforced: check_answer_condition refuses grounded_answer together with required_effects or required_answer, and acceptance_met keeps a grounded end from meeting any other spec. Three gaps remain. (a) Registry admission accepts a task definition that sets acceptance.grounded_answer while its capabilities include an EffectKind.WRITE, or while its budgets.max_admitted_writes is above 0. (b) _admits_grounded_answer refuses only an offered set that holds a typed answer (EffectKind.ANSWER). An unbound run whose agent-visible set includes a write (the notes pack, 'write standup note') is offered cite_and_answer and can end SUCCEEDED/GROUNDED in place of its write. (c) _handle_grounded_answer never checks for an earlier write proposal in the run, blocked or reserved. Before Phase 3, run_loop Ruling 3 kept a run that had read something from ending SUCCEEDED without a VERIFIED action. This follows the letter of ADR 0033 section 3 (its three admission conditions), but not the brief's invariant or the ADR's 'read-only question' purpose. The discriminator to rule on: no EffectKind.WRITE in the offered set, or max_admitted_writes == 0, checked at admission of the run and of the definition. Fix: add that condition, or get an owner ruling that amends ADR 0033 section 3. Not on the live write path. Every committed profile pins grounded_answers off (test_committed_profiles_keep_phase3_toggles_off; fixture_profile.json:96, dev-ollama.json:106, live.example.json:111). Unbound ERP runs never admit, because ERP offers typed answers. open-pos v2 is read-only, with max_admitted_writes 0.

After a kernel_repeat on fallback (and a typed-answer grounding fallback), the run record that record_fallback returns is thrown away, so _handle_proposal carries on with the pre-fallback revision. Only the rationale probe's fallback is threaded back (run = reasons.run or run). The writes I checked re-read the run (_await_approval, the blocked branch, _handle_answer's failure branch), so I found no failure, but the execution_ir shadow/on calls that take run were not traced. Threading the returned run, as the rationale probe does, would make this robust.
